title: How to Design an Infographic Slide in PowerPoint (Templates Included)
excerpt: Learn how to design a professional infographic slide in PowerPoint with step-by-step guidance, slide design tips, and free PowerPoint infographic templates to get started fast.
html:
Learning how to design an infographic slide in PowerPoint is one of the highest-leverage skills in corporate communication. Most business decks fail because they treat slides as documents to be read rather than visual aids to support a spoken talk. The result is a wall of 12pt bullets that the speaker reads aloud, which is the fastest way to lose a room. This guide walks through how to design professional infographic slides in PowerPoint — with layout grids, typography rules, and free templates to get started.

Slides Versus Documents: The Distance Rule

The primary reason PowerPoint infographic slides fail is because presenters copy-paste charts or layouts designed for reports directly onto slides.

* A report document is read six inches from the reader's eyes, at their own pace. It can handle high data density and paragraphs of text.

* A projected slide is read fifteen feet from the audience's eyes, while they are listening to you speak. It must be simple, bold, and readable in under five seconds.

To design a slide that works, you must enlarge every element. Make titles at least 36pt, body text 20pt, chart lines 3pt thick, and remove gridlines. If your content won't fit at these sizes, you have too much text. Cut the copy, not the font size.

Designing the Layout Grid

A professional slide relies on a structured grid to align elements and create visual hierarchy.

* Use a 3-column grid for lists, steps, or comparing three items. It is the most versatile corporate slide layout.

* Use a 2-column grid for head-to-head comparisons or linking a key visual with a short text block.

* Use a horizontal layout for timelines, Gantt roadmaps, and process steps.

Set your slide size to Widescreen (16:9) in Page Setup before you design. Widescreen is the standard for modern projectors and monitors.

Applying Color and Typography

Two design choices that immediately separate professional slides from default templates:

1. Two fonts maximum. Use one clean sans-serif for titles (like Arial, Segoe UI, or a custom brand font) and one readable sans-serif for body copy (like Calibri or Open Sans). Never mix serifs and sans-serifs unless your brand guidelines explicitly require it.

2. Color restraint. Use one dark neutral color (like charcoal or dark navy) for text and gridlines, and one bright brand color (like orange or blue) to highlight the key data point. If every bar is a different color, the slide becomes visual noise.

Keep these rules consistent across every slide in your deck to maintain a professional look.

Building the Slide in PowerPoint

Follow these steps to build your slide:

1. Rebuild charts for projection distance. Enlarge labels to 18pt and remove legends.

2. Label data series directly on the chart lines or bars.

3. Replace paragraphs of text with short phrases and large KPI callouts.

4. Add data source lines at the bottom of the slide.

5. Review the slide from the back of the room before presenting.

PowerPoint slides work best when they focus on a single message. Rebuild your charts for projection distance, use a structured layout grid, restrict your color palette, and write titles that state your conclusion. See our Chart Types Guide for help matching your data to the right format.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a PowerPoint infographic slide?

A PowerPoint infographic slide is a presentation slide that uses visual elements like charts, icons, process diagrams, and large numbers to communicate data or workflows clearly and quickly. It replaces standard bulleted lists with structured layouts that support the speaker's narrative.

How do I make a PowerPoint infographic slide for free?

Start with a free infographic slide template in PowerPoint or Canva — search "infographic slide" to browse editable layouts. Swap the template's placeholder text with your content, update the colors to match your brand, and ensure all alignment matches the grid. You can download free templates on IllustrateWords.

What is the optimal font size for PowerPoint slides?

Titles: 36–48pt minimum. Body text: 20–24pt minimum. Captions and source credits: 14–16pt minimum. If your text won't fit at these sizes, cut the words. Do not lower the font size, or the slide will become unreadable from the back of the room.

Should I use icons on my PowerPoint slides?

Yes, but use them consistently. Pick one icon style (such as flat outline or filled color) and use it across the entire deck. Icons should clarify a category or action (like a folder for "Organization" or a chart for "Growth"), not just decorate empty space on the slide.

How do I align elements on a PowerPoint slide?

Use PowerPoint's built-in "Align" tools (Home → Arrange → Align) to distribute elements evenly across the slide. Never eyeball spacing; minor misalignments are highly visible to an audience and make slides look unprofessional.
